questions.question: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the thumb is directed towards the direction of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b72937cf535ccde879f48f3c0a69560cb6e29a846b9275f66f205b5affbd5db4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right-Hand Thumb Rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field relative to the direction of the current.
 
• In this rule, the thumb points in the direction of the current, and the fingers curl around the conductor, indicating the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The Right-Hand Thumb Rule helps visualize the 3-dimensional relationship between current and magnetic fields, crucial in electromagnetism.
 
• This rule is fundamental in understanding the behavior of electromagnets, electric motors, and generators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current**

 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge in a conductor, typically measured in amperes (A).
 
• It is the movement of electrons through a conductive material, such as a wire.
 
• The direction of conventional current is taken as the direction in which positive charge carriers would move.
 
• In most practical scenarios, electrons (negative charge carriers) move in the opposite direction to the conventional current.
 
 
 
• **Electric Field**
 
 
• An electric field is a region around a charged particle or object within which a force would be exerted on other charged particles or objects.
 
• It is represented by field lines that point in the direction a positive test charge would move if placed in the field.
 
• The strength of the electric field is measured in volts per meter (V/m).
 
• Electric fields are fundamental to the behavior of electric charges and the operation of capacitors.
 
 
 
• **Motion of the Conductor**
 
 
• The motion of a conductor in a magnetic field induces a voltage across the conductor.
 
• This phenomenon is described by Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction.
 
• The direction of the induced voltage is given by Lenz's Law, which states that the induced voltage will oppose the change in magnetic flux.
 
• This principle is applied in the operation of electric generators.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field**
 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• It is represented by field lines that indicate the direction and strength of the magnetic force.
 
• The strength of a magnetic field is measured in teslas (T) or gauss (G).
 
• Magnetic fields are fundamental to the operation of electromagnets, transformers, and magnetic storage devices.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution CANNOT be suspended even during an emergency declared on the grounds of war or external aggression?

• Both Articles 20 and 21 are fundamental rights under Part III of the Indian Constitution and remain enforceable during times of emergency.

questions.question: What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India?

options.text: Ensuring food security in the western states
Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Focusing on holistic development in agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Green Revolution aimed at **enhancing productivity** sustainably through modern agricultural practices.
 
• It focused on **diversification** of crops, not just staple cereals, to ensure a balanced growth in agriculture.
 
• The initiative aimed to **integrate technology** and innovation in farming, including the use of biotechnology and precision farming.
 
• It also emphasized **improving the income** of farmers by promoting value addition, market linkages, and reducing the cost of cultivation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The term "Green Revolution" refers to a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s.
 
• It involved the development of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, increased use of fertilizers and irrigation methods, which significantly boosted agricultural production in many developing countries, including India.
 
 
 
• **Biotechnology in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Biotechnology refers to the use of living organisms or their systems to develop or make products. In agriculture, it includes genetic engineering, molecular markers, molecular diagnostics, vaccines, and tissue culture.
 
• It helps in developing crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, reducing the need for chemical pesticides, and enhancing the nutritional value of crops.
 
 
 
• **Precision Farming:**
 
 
• Precision farming is an agricultural management concept based on observing, measuring, and responding to inter and intra-field variability in crops.
 
• It involves the use of technologies like GPS, sensors, and data analytics to optimize field-level management with regard to crop farming.
 
 
 
• **Value Addition in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Value addition refers to the process of changing or transforming a product from its original state to a more valuable state.
 
• In agriculture, it involves processes such as cleaning, sorting, grading, processing, packaging, and branding which enhance the marketability and profitability of agricultural produce.

questions.question: In Newlands' Octaves, the properties of lithium and _______ were found to be the same.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newlands' Octaves was an early attempt to classify the elements.
 
• John Newlands observed that when elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element were similar.
 
• In Newlands' Octaves, lithium and sodium showed similar properties.
 
• This observation was one of the early pieces of evidence that led to the development of the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newlands' Octaves:**

 
 
• Newlands' Octaves was proposed by John Newlands in 1864.
 
• It is based on the observation that elements exhibit similar properties at every eighth element when arranged by increasing atomic mass.
 
• This was analogous to the octaves in music, where every eighth note is similar to the first.
 
• Although this system had limitations and was not applicable to elements beyond calcium, it was an important step towards the development of the modern periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number, not atomic mass.
 
• It was developed by Dmitri Mendeleev and later refined by Henry Moseley.
 
• The periodic table is divided into periods (rows) and groups (columns).
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Alkali Metals (Group 1):**
 
 
• Group 1 elements (alkali metals) include lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, cesium, and francium.
 
• These metals are highly reactive, especially with water, and form strong alkaline hydroxides.
 
• They have one electron in their outermost shell, which they readily lose to form +1 ions.
 
• They are soft metals with low melting points and are good conductors of electricity.

questions.question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MV=PT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fisher's equation of exchange is represented as **MV=PT**.
 
• In this equation, **M** stands for the money supply in an economy.
 
• **V** represents the velocity of money, which is the rate at which money circulates in the economy.
 
• **P** is the price level, and **T** represents the total volume of transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Supply (M)**

 
 
• The total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.
 
• It includes various components such as currency in circulation and demand deposits.
 
• Changes in the money supply can influence inflation, interest rates, and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Velocity of Money (V)**
 
 
• The rate at which money is exchanged from one transaction to another.
 
• It indicates the efficiency of money in an economy; a higher velocity means money is changing hands more frequently.
 
• Velocity is calculated as the ratio of nominal GDP to the money supply.
 
 
 
• **Price Level (P)**
 
 
• The average of current prices across the entire spectrum of goods and services produced in the economy.
 
• It is often measured by price indices such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the GDP deflator.
 
• Changes in the price level reflect inflation or deflation in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Total Volume of Transactions (T)**
 
 
• The total number of transactions or the total quantity of goods and services traded in the economy.
 
• This can include consumer spending, business investments, and government expenditures.
 
• The volume of transactions is an indicator of economic activity.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts passed under Warren Hastings was also called 'half-loaf system'?

The correct answer is __**Pitt’s India Act 1784.**__

__
 
• Pitt's India Act 1784

 
 
• This Act, also known as the East India Company Act 1784, established dual control of British territories in India by the British government and the East India Company.
 
• The Act created a Board of Control to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the company, enhancing the British government's authority.
 
• It marked a significant step towards the establishment of British rule in India.
 
• The Pitt's India Act of 1784, also known as the East India Company Act of 1784, is sometimes referred to as the **"half-loaf system"**. This act established a dual system of governance in India, separating the political and commercial functions of the East India Company.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act 1773**

 
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step taken by the British government to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It was passed by the British Parliament to establish a system of governance for British territories in India.
 
• The Act created the position of Governor-General of Bengal and was the precursor to the later Governor-General of India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary control over the East India Company, transitioning from purely commercial to political governance.
 
 

 
• **Government of India Act 1858**

 
 
• This Act, passed after the Indian Rebellion of 1857, resulted in the British Crown assuming direct control over India, ending the rule of the East India Company.
 
• It established the office of the Secretary of State for India and the India Council to assist in governance.
 
• The Governor-General of India was now called the Viceroy, representing the British monarch.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act 1813**
 
 
• This Act renewed the East India Company's charter but ended its monopoly on trade with India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• It allowed other British merchants to trade with India, increasing competition and economic activity.
 
• The Act also provided for the promotion of education and the Christian religion in India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas’?

__
 
• **Article 43** of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It states that **'The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas'**.
 
• The objective of this article is to promote economic growth and self-sufficiency in rural areas.
 
• It aims to provide economic opportunities and employment in rural areas through the promotion of small-scale industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The DPSP are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles are aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• While they are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Cottage Industries**
 
 
• Cottage industries are small-scale, decentralized manufacturing businesses often operated out of a home rather than a purpose-built facility.
 
• They typically involve the production of handmade goods and are labor-intensive.
 
• These industries play a vital role in the economy by providing employment and promoting traditional crafts.
 
• In rural areas, cottage industries help in reducing unemployment and migration to urban areas by providing local employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Rural Development**
 
 
• Rural development involves improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas, often relatively isolated and sparsely populated areas.
 
• It focuses on the development of infrastructure, education, healthcare, and employment opportunities.
 
• Promoting cottage industries is one way to achieve rural development by utilizing local resources and skills.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President's rule in an state?

__
 
• Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with the imposition of President's Rule in states.
 
• This article is also known as the "President's Rule" or "State Emergency."
 
• It allows the President of India to take over the functions of the state government if the state government is unable to function according to the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• President's Rule can be imposed for a maximum period of six months at a time and can be extended with the approval of the Parliament, but not beyond three years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352**

 
 
• Article 352 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation of National Emergency.
 
• It can be declared due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• During a National Emergency, the central government gains sweeping powers, and the state governments come under the direct control of the central government.
 
• This can be proclaimed by the President of India based on the written advice of the Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Article 358**
 
 
• Article 358 provides for the suspension of the rights guaranteed by Article 19 during a National Emergency.
 
• It states that while a National Emergency is in operation, nothing in Article 19 shall restrict the power of the State to make any law or to take any executive action abridging or taking away the rights conferred by Article 19.
 
 
 
• **Article 360**
 
 
• Article 360 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation of Financial Emergency.
 
• The President can declare a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to giving directions to any state to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions.
 
• However, no Financial Emergency has been declared in India so far.

questions.question: In a kite ABCD, the longer diagonal BD is drawn. If ∠ABD = 54° and ∠ADB = 50°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of the ∠DCB ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a kite, if a diagonal splits unequal adjacent angles (∠ABD ≠ ∠ADB), it must be the axis of symmetry.

This means the diagonal BD divides the kite into two identical triangles, making ∠C = ∠A.

In ΔABD, the sum of all angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠A = 180° − (54° + 50°) = 76°

⇒ ∠C = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a kite.

∠ABD = 54°

∠ADB = 50°

**Method Used:**

A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides, and its main diagonal divides it into two congruent triangles.

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is always 180°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5df2020eaca75367f4ac4cbf7c9fae51ee9639caa0161506738769cd0f5eee5c.png] 

⇒ For the given kite ABCD, if AB were equal to AD, ΔABD would be an isosceles triangle, making ∠ABD = ∠ADB.

⇒ However, given ∠ABD (54°) ≠ ∠ADB (50°), we conclude that AB ≠ AD.

⇒ Therefore, the adjacent equal sides must be AB = BC and AD = CD.

⇒ In this configuration, the diagonal BD acts as the axis of symmetry.

⇒ Because BD is the axis of symmetry, it divides the kite into two congruent triangles: ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD.

⇒ In ΔABD, the sum of internal angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠DAB + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB + 54° + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB + 104° = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB = 180° − 104° = 76°

⇒ Due to the exact congruence of ΔABD and ΔCBD, the corresponding angles are perfectly equal, meaning ∠DCB = ∠DAB.

⇒ ∠DCB = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Kite

A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal-length sides that are adjacent to each other. The opposite angles where the unequal sides meet are always equal.

Diagonals of a Kite

The diagonals of a kite are always perpendicular to each other, intersecting at exactly 90°. The main diagonal (axis of symmetry) acts as the perpendicular bisector of the other diagonal.

Axis of Symmetry

The diagonal connecting the common vertices of the equal sides acts as the axis of symmetry. It bisects the angles at its endpoints and cleanly divides the kite into two identical congruent triangles.

questions.question: Three candidates X, Y and Z participated in an election. X got 30% more votes than Y, whereas Z got 25% more votes than Y. X also overtook Z by 5000 votes. If 71% of the voters voted and no invalid votes were cast, then what was the total number of voters in the voting list?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Y = 100 units ⇒ X = 130 units and Z = 125 units.

Difference (X − Z) = 130 − 125 = 5 units → 5000 votes.

Total cast votes = X + Y + Z = 130 + 100 + 125 = 355 units.

Total cast votes = 355 × (5000 ÷ 5) = 3,55,000.

Total voters list = (3,55,000 ÷ 71) × 100 = 5,00,000.

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = 130% of Y, Z = 125% of Y, X − Z = 5000, Cast votes = 71% of Total list.

**Formula Used:**

Number of votes = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base value; Total Voters = (Cast Votes ÷ Cast Percentage) × 100.

 
 Y (100u)

Percentage Comparison

Given the sum of the sides a + b = 9 and their product ab = 18.

By finding two numbers that add up to 9 and multiply to 18, we can easily identify the sides as a = 6 and b = 3.

We need to find the value of (a² − ab + b²).

Substitute the values directly: 6² − (6 × 3) + 3²

⇒ 36 − 18 + 9 = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Breadth of the rectangular field = b

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

From the standard algebraic identity, we can modify the required expression as follows:

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (a² + b² + 2ab) − 3ab

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (a + b)² − 3ab

Now, substitute the given values (a + b = 9 and ab = 18) into the modified equation:

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (9)² − 3 × 18

⇒ a² − ab + b² = 81 − 54

⇒ a² − ab + b² = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

questions.question: If tanθ = 5/8, then find the value of ((1 + cos theta)(1 - cos theta))/((1 + sin theta)(1 - sin theta))
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is [(1 + cos θ) × (1 − cos θ)] ÷ [(1 + sin θ) × (1 − sin θ)]

Using the algebraic identity (a + b) × (a − b) = a² − b², the expression becomes (1 − cos² θ) ÷ (1 − sin² θ)

Using the fundamental trigonometric identities, we know that 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ and 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ

Substituting these, Expression = sin² θ ÷ cos² θ = tan² θ

Since tan θ = 5/8, we get (5/8)² = 25/64

**∴ The correct answer is 25/64.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** tan θ = 5/8

We know that tan θ = Perpendicular (P) ÷ Base (B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb178536f707fc321e1f68c1aee2a561db42e288f323ef56eb293bb91e4656c5.png] 

⇒ Let Perpendicular P = 5 and Base B = 8

**Formula Used:** Pythagoras Theorem: H² = P² + B²

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(5² + 8²)

⇒ H = √(25 + 64) = √89

⇒ sin θ = P ÷ H = 5/√89

⇒ cos θ = B ÷ H = 8/√89

Now, evaluate the given expression:

⇒ [(1 + cos θ) × (1 − cos θ)] ÷ [(1 + sin θ) × (1 − sin θ)]

⇒ [(1 + 8/√89) × (1 − 8/√89)] ÷ [(1 + 5/√89) × (1 − 5/√89)]

⇒ [1 − (8/√89)²] ÷ [1 − (5/√89)²]

⇒ [1 − 64/89] ÷ [1 − 25/89]

⇒ [(89 − 64) ÷ 89] ÷ [(89 − 25) ÷ 89]

⇒ (25/89) ÷ (64/89)

⇒ 25/64

**∴ The correct answer is 25/64.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental Pythagorean identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Algebraic Identities

The difference of squares formula (a + b) × (a − b) = a² − b² is highly useful for simplifying conjugate trigonometric expressions.

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.
</p

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time taken by both to meet is the same, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds = Policeman : Thief = 27 : 22

Difference in ratio = 27 − 22 = 5 units

This 5 units represents the initial gap of 195 m ⇒ 1 unit = 195 ÷ 5 = 39 m

Distance covered by the thief = 22 units = 22 × 39 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 195 m

Speed of Policeman (SP) = 27 km/h

Speed of Thief (ST) = 22 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 27 − 22 = 5 km/h

⇒ Convert Relative Speed into m/s = 5 × (5 ÷ 18) = 25 ÷ 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken by Policeman to overtake = 195 ÷ (25 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = (195 × 18) ÷ 25 = 140.4 seconds

⇒ Speed of Thief in m/s = 22 × (5 ÷ 18) = 55 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the Thief = Speed × Time = (55 ÷ 9) × 140.4

⇒ Distance = 55 × 15.6 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is their sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

If the time taken is constant, the distance traveled by an object is directly proportional to its speed (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂). This allows solving chase problems instantly using ratio methods.

⇒ Initial Girls = 6 units = 6 × 120 = 720
